answer.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious move, but the one inherited memory supporting it (memory_73) carries an explicit self-flagged defect: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' may be an artifact of cohort mixing rather than a real effect. Discount-led acquisition also has a known downstream value risk against the stated objective — price-matching a cheaper entrant tends to recruit discount-conditioned accounts whose expansion and retention are weaker, so a headline acquisition win can degrade sustainable qualified revenue. That is exactly the wrong bet to make on a single non-recurring slot. Meanwhile the actual observed damage is internal, not competitive: onboarding completion is down 4% and activation down 6% QoQ, and these are causally linked — memory_86 says shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value, and weak onboarding completion plausibly propagates into the activation decline, so repairing onboarding may recover both metrics rather than one. memory_31 and memory_91 corroborate the same funnel region from independent tests, giving the onboarding/activation thesis triangulated support that memory_73 lacks. I choose simplify_onboarding over activation_messaging because it sits upstream of activation and thus addresses the likely root cause instead of a symptom. Verification spend: memory_73 to see whether the pricing lift survives de-pooling (if it does, that materially changes next week's ranking, so the information is worth buying even though I am not acting on it now) and memory_86 to confirm the completion/time-to-value lift was measured on a comparable self-serve population and was durable rather than a one-off. Standard experiment scale, not broad rollout: the inherited results are encouraging but are prior-generation reads on a pre-decline funnel, and I should not assume the current 4-6% deterioration shares the same mechanism. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving: whether the SMB losses are genuinely price-driven (in which case funnel repair alone will not hold that segment) and whether referral_incentive's clean result in memory_57 transfers to a base under active competitive attrition. If verification shows memory_86's effect was narrow or stale, I would fall back to activation_messaging rather than to pricing.
